headline: Wood products strength offsets a land-solutions pullback
summary_short: Weyerhaeuser posted Q2 FY2026 net earnings of $162M ($0.23 diluted EPS), up sharply y/y from $87M ($0.12) largely on a $71M after-tax Oregon timberland-sale gain, while Adjusted EBITDA of $310M fell 7.7% y/y as Wood Products' gains didn't fully offset weaker Timberlands and land-solutions results.
summary_long: Net earnings rose to $162M ($0.23 diluted EPS) from $87M ($0.12) y/y, driven by a $71M after-tax gain on June's Oregon timberland sale; before special items, diluted EPS was $0.13 vs $0.12. Revenue of $1,867M rose 8.1% q/q on stronger Wood Products pricing (lumber +15%, OSB +3% q/q) but slipped 0.9% y/y. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $310M from $336M y/y as Timberlands EBITDA dropped to $123M from $152M and Strategic Land Solutions cooled after a one-off Q1 gain, while Wood Products EBITDA nearly doubled to $129M. Cash rose to $527M on $399M operating cash flow plus $114M of sale proceeds. Strategic Land Solutions FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance raised $25M to ~$450M.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites solid operating performance across businesses, continued optimization of the timberlands portfolio, and an encouraging recent uptick in lumber and western log pricing despite macro and inflationary headwinds.
Wood Products led the q/q gain: lumber and OSB sales realizations rose 15% and 3% respectively vs Q1 averages, with higher sales volumes across lumber, engineered wood products, and distribution.
Driven by a $71M after-tax special-item gain on the Oregon timberland sale not present a year earlier; before special items, diluted EPS was $0.13 vs $0.12, a much smaller y/y move.
Reflects the same $71M after-tax special-item land-sale gain plus stronger Wood Products results, partly offset by Strategic Land Solutions' loss of a one-off Q1 conservation-easement gain.
Wood Products operating contribution nearly doubled to $71M from $42M q/q on higher realizations, and this quarter includes a $71M special-item land-sale gain within Timberlands.
Not explained in the release as a standalone line; per SEC-XBRL figures, revenue fell 0.9% y/y while cost of sales held roughly flat, compressing gross profit.
Per the company's own segment reconciliation, Timberlands EBITDA fell to $123M from $152M y/y and unallocated items worsened to -$71M from -$60M, outweighing Wood Products' rise to $129M from $101M.
Cash rose to $527M from $299M at Q1-end on $399M of net cash from operations plus $114M of proceeds from the Oregon timberland divestiture completed in June.
Not explained in the release; a roughly flat q/q balance is consistent with net income retained being largely offset by shareholder distributions.
